vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: baoyu-post-to-weibo
Version: 1.115.4

The skill bundle implements Weibo automation using high-risk system-level interactions, including global keystroke simulation and clipboard manipulation via platform-specific tools like osascript (macOS), PowerShell (Windows), and xdotool (Linux) in scripts like paste-from-clipboard.ts and copy-to-clipboard.ts. Furthermore, SKILL.md contains explicit instructions for the AI agent to automatically kill Chrome processes and retry commands without user confirmation when encountering specific errors. While these capabilities are plausibly required to bypass anti-bot detection and handle complex web editors, they provide a powerful primitive for unauthorized system interaction if the agent is manipulated via prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its Weibo-posting purpose, but it explicitly uses logged-in Chrome automation to bypass anti-bot detection and runs OS-level clipboard/keystroke commands.

dimensions.detail: Posting text, media, and articles to Weibo is coherent with the stated purpose, and the artifacts say the user manually publishes; however, the skill also advertises using real Chrome to bypass anti-bot detection, which is a material safety and account-risk concern.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions are generally scoped to composing Weibo content for user review. The automatic troubleshooting step is limited to killing CDP Chrome instances for the skill profile, not all Chrome processes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec. The skill runs TypeScript scripts with bun or an unpinned `npx -y bun` fallback and uses external packages listed in `scripts/package.json` with a lockfile present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses Chrome CDP, local file upload, system clipboard control, and real paste keystrokes. Much of this is purpose-aligned for rich Weibo composition, but combined with anti-bot bypass language it is higher risk than a simple posting helper.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill relies on a persistent Chrome profile with a saved Weibo login session. This is expected for browser-based Weibo posting, but users should prefer a dedicated profile.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing, make sure you are comfortable letting the skill drive a logged-in Chrome session and use your clipboard/keystrokes to compose Weibo content. Use a dedicated Chrome profile, review all text and media in the browser before clicking publish, avoid switching apps while it runs, and prefer a trusted local Bun installation over the npx fallback.
llm.findings:
[suspicious.dangerous_exec] expected: `scripts/copy-to-clipboard.ts` uses `child_process.spawn` to call platform clipboard tools and generated Swift/PowerShell helpers; this is expected for cross-platform clipboard support but has OS-level effects.
[suspicious.dangerous_exec] expected: `scripts/paste-from-clipboard.ts` uses `spawnSync` for osascript, xdotool/ydotool, and PowerShell SendKeys to send paste keystrokes; this is expected for the described browser paste workflow but can affect the active app if focus is wrong.
[suspicious.dangerous_exec] expected: The provided static scan snippet for `scripts/weibo-utils.ts` shows `execSync('cmd.exe /C "echo %USERPROFILE%"')`, which appears to be Windows profile-path discovery; the full file was not included in the visible artifact text.

evidence.explanation: The skill advertises browser automation specifically as a way to bypass anti-bot detection while preparing public social-media posts.
evidence.snippet: Posts text, images, videos, and long-form articles to Weibo via real Chrome browser (bypasses anti-bot detection).

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Install only if you are comfortable with browser automation against Weibo. Keep the manual review step, avoid using it to evade platform protections, and consider using a dedicated Weibo account/profile.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Using this may put the user's Weibo account or content at risk if Weibo treats the automation as evasion, even though the artifact says the final publish click is manual.

evidence.explanation: The skill relies on a saved browser session to act as the user's logged-in Weibo account.
evidence.snippet: First run: log in to Weibo manually (session saved)

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Use a dedicated Chrome profile for this skill, review the browser before publishing, and log out or remove the profile if you no longer want the skill to have account access.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Anyone or any agent process using the same configured Chrome profile could compose content under the logged-in Weibo account.

evidence.explanation: The helper runs OS automation commands to send paste keystrokes to the frontmost or targeted application.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Watch the browser while the skill runs, avoid switching apps during paste steps, and stop the run if the wrong application is focused.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: If focus is wrong, the skill could paste article content or images into an unintended application.

evidence.explanation: If Bun is not installed, the documented runtime fallback can download and run a package via npx. This is a common setup pattern but relies on external package provenance.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Prefer installing Bun from a trusted source and review or preserve the provided lockfile for the script dependencies.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Running through npx may fetch runtime code from the package registry at execution time.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: The main concern is explicit anti-bot-bypass browser automation; OS command and clipboard automation are purpose-aligned but powerful.

permission_boundary.summary: The skill uses a persistent logged-in Weibo browser session, which is expected but should be isolated to a dedicated profile.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: No artifact-backed evidence of hidden data exfiltration or cross-agent sensitive-data sharing was found in the provided artifacts.
